text:
rachel: FWIW our edge onboarding sample just caused another downstream typing surprise. Consumers importing the ESM entry see SDK generics collapse to `any`/`unknown`. Runtime is fine.

dom: is this the same wrapper issue where we replace `export function` with `const fn = makeFn()`? That often kills overloads in emitted .d.ts.

rachel: exactly. Minimal failing sketch from SDK before bundle: 
```ts
export function exec<T>(path: string, opts?: O): Promise<T>
export function exec(path: string, opts?: O): Promise<any>
```
After our build+wrapping the consumer's editor shows `Promise<any>` even when they call `exec<MyType>(...)`.

li: reproducible across TS 5.x with `module: "esnext"` and `moduleResolution: "bundler"`?
rachel: yes, tested on TS 5.2/5.3 with bundler mode. Hand-editing a preserved .d.ts with `declare function exec<T>(...)` fixes inference.

dom: short-term: publish a types-only ESM d.ts that preserves `declare function` overloads before the wrapper transform. Also add an onboarding tsconfig example for edge: users can copy/paste and avoid common flags that interact poorly.

li: also add a small CI consumer compile check in the repo: create a toy package that imports the ESM entry and run `tsc --noEmit` across a matrix (moduleResolution: bundler, node16/node18). That will catch regressions.

types-bot: Suggested test: assert that `tsc --noEmit` on consumer project succeeds and that `node_modules/@redwood/sdk/types.d.ts` contains `declare function exec<` for the ESM entry.

rachel: long-term: refactor away from overlapping overloads where possible. Use a single generic signature with discriminated opts so TS never has to choose between a generic and non-generic overload.

dom: implementation note: when generating types from wrapper factories, prefer `declare function`/`export { exec }` pattern in the types artifact instead of `const exec: typeof createExec(...)`. The latter loses the declaration overloads.

li: agree. I'll prototype the preserved types artifact and add the CI consumer job. dom: want to own the refactor for the most-used APIs?
dom: I'll take the refactor after the preserved-types patch lands.

devex-bot: Created ticket INF-10234 "edge ESM typing emission: overloads collapse to any/unknown after wrapper transform" assigned to @li, @dom; priority: P2 :thumbsup:

rachel: I'll post the tiny repro repo and failing `tsc --noEmit` command in the ticket. Also adding an onboarding note that `skipLibCheck` is not a fix, and listing the recommended tsconfig snippet.
